item.title: Implement ledger.py per SPEC.md with focused tests
item.brief:
Operator request, verbatim: "Implement `ledger.py` according to `SPEC.md`. Preserve the documented API, handle every specified error and boundary case, and add focused tests. The existing tests cover basics only. Use the Python standard library and commit your work."

Context: repository quality-ledger-transfer, base branch main. Read SPEC.md in full first and treat it as the contract: implement every documented function, class and behaviour, keep the documented API exactly as written, and handle every specified error and boundary case explicitly (raise the specified exception types; do not swallow errors).

Tests: extend the existing test suite with focused tests covering each specified error path and boundary case, not only the basics. Use the standard library only (unittest or pytest-free unittest; no new third-party dependencies). Run the full test suite and make sure it passes before committing.

Code rules: keep functions under 60 lines, validate inputs at boundaries with clear errors, no bare or silent except blocks, no unnecessary comments, no unneeded abstractions.

Git: commit the work on the current branch with the repository's configured git identity. Do not override the git user, and do not add any attribution line such as "Co-Authored-By" or "Generated with" to the commit message. Push nothing.

state.summary:
Implemented ledger.py per SPEC.md and extended test_ledger.py to cover every specified error path, boundary and threading case. Committed as 65b8fa5 on archon/cewr210e-implement-ledger-py-per-spec-md-with-foc under the configured identity (mengsig); nothing pushed.

What changed: Ledger validates balances at construction (dict only, nonempty string names, built-in ints in [0, MAX_BALANCE], bools rejected) and copies its input. transfer validates the amount first (built-in int in [1, MAX_BALANCE]), then raises KeyError for unknown accounts, then returns False on insufficient funds or destination overflow without changing anything. Same-account transfers return True iff funds suffice and never change balances. All operations take one per-ledger lock, so transfers are atomic and opposite transfers cannot deadlock. snapshot returns a copy.

Checks: `python3 -B -m unittest test_ledger` ran 30 tests, all OK, three runs in my worktree; the reviewer also ran it three times and once under -O, all OK. No linter is installed here, so no lint was run. Full tree 786cdebd127c78476ac16819f4808ac7e32506a7.

Risk: high. The change adds a lock around all balance mutation and snapshot. Threaded tests are sized to finish in seconds, but they were not stress-tested on free-threaded CPython. I proceeded rather than escalating because the module is new and self-contained, and the lock is the spec's own requirement.

Review: one reviewer (agt_01M7W82RG63FHJ9TA228SZA6RM) passed the head with no blocking findings. Two non-blocking follow-ups: add a test that a non-string destination (e.g. None) raises KeyError; rename test_failed_transfer_keeps_total, which duplicates the overflow case.

REVIEW: pass, by claude-code/claude-haiku-5-5 (agent agt_01M7W82RG63FHJ9TA228SZA6RM)

SHIPPED: commit 65b8fa5c7b64ce098bdc5daae1ae5045c346b515 on the run branch

evidence.none: Pure library implementation with no visible or measurable change; behaviour is covered by unit tests.

pr.body: Approach: single per-ledger threading.Lock guards transfer and snapshot; account membership checks run before the lock (keys are never removed). Key files: ledger.py, test_ledger.py. Checks: unittest, 30 tests OK across repeated runs. No linter installed. Assumptions: non-str account names raise KeyError on transfer (unhashable included); whitespace-only names are accepted as nonempty. Follow-ups (non-blocking): test None destination -> KeyError; rename test_failed_transfer_keeps_total. Not verified: free-threaded CPython stress.
pr.summary: Made atomic, validated account transfers possible. Now: Ledger enforces SPEC error types, bounds and same-account rules under one lock, with 30 tests. Before: ledger.py was a NotImplementedError stub with 2 basic tests.
pr.title: Implement thread-safe Ledger per SPEC.md with focused tests

risk.why: Concurrency and locking around all balance mutation. Lock use reviewed for deadlock; threaded tests pass but no stress beyond test sizes. Only ledger.py and test_ledger.py touched; new module, no existing code depends on it.
